The joy of learning R is that you can learn anything as long as you put the time. R is free, so is RStudio. Most books on R are also free, and have wonderful online versions you can consult.

Below a list of my favourite online resources on R, organised by topic:

::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon="false"}
## Bookmark this!

-   [Statistical Modeling, Causal Inference, and Social Science Blog](https://statmodeling.stat.columbia.edu/)

-   [Andrew Heiss' Blog](https://www.andrewheiss.com/blog/) 

-   [Telling stories with data](https://tellingstorieswithdata.com/)

-   [R for Data Science 1st edition](https://r4ds.had.co.nz/) and [2nd edition](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/)

-   [Introduction to Data Science](https://rafalab.github.io/dsbook/)

-   [R Programming for Data Science](https://bookdown.org/rdpeng/rprogdatascience/)

-   [Hands-On Programming with R](https://rstudio-education.github.io/hopr/)

-   [Big Book of R](https://www.bigbookofr.com/)

-   [Solomon Kurz's Blog](https://solomonkurz.netlify.app/blog/)
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon="false"}
## Mapping

-   [Geocomputation with R](https://geocompr.robinlovelace.net/)

-   [Spatial Data Science](https://rspatial.org/raster/#)

-   [Leaflet for R](https://rstudio.github.io/leaflet/)
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon="false"}
## Visualisation

-   [R Graphics Cookbook](https://r-graphics.org/)

-   [Fundamentals of Data Visualization](https://clauswilke.com/dataviz/)

-   [Interactive web-based data visualization with R, plotly, and shiny](https://plotly-r.com/)

-   [ggiraph book](https://www.ardata.fr/ggiraph-book/)
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon="false"}
## Text analysis

-   [Text mining with R](https://www.tidytextmining.com/)

-   [Supervised Machine Learning for text analysis in R](https://smltar.com/)
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon="false"}
## Publishing

-   [Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/reference/)

-   [R Markdown Cookbook](https://bookdown.org/yihui/rmarkdown-cookbook/)

-   [R Markdown: The Definitive Guide](https://bookdown.org/yihui/rmarkdown/)

:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon="false"}
## Shiny

-   [Mastering Shiny](https://mastering-shiny.org/)

-   [Outstanding User Interfaces with Shiny](https://unleash-shiny.rinterface.com/)
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon="false"}
## LLMs & AI

-   [ellmer](https://ellmer.tidyverse.org/) --call any LLM from R

-   [shinychat](https://posit-dev.github.io/shinychat/r/) and [querychat](https://posit-dev.github.io/querychat/r/) --chat UIs and natural-language data querying for Shiny

-   [ggsql](https://r.ggsql.org/) --grammar of graphics for SQL (alpha)

-   [Large Language Model tools for R](https://luisdva.github.io/llmsr-book/) --a free book cataloguing the whole ecosystem

-   [Posit's AI tools overview](https://opensource.posit.co/ai/)
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon="false"}
## Causal inference

-   [*Causal Inference: The Mixtape*](https://mixtape.scunning.com/) by Scott Cunningham

-   [*The Effect: An Introduction to Research Design and Causality*](https://theeffectbook.net/) by Nick Huntington-Klein

-   [The DAG Almanac](https://dags.andrewheiss.com/) by Andrew Heiss --interactive DAGs and do-calculus

-   [Understanding adjustment](https://rpsychologist.com/descriptive-adjustment/) by Kristoffer Magnusson

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon="false"}
## Statistics

-   [Statistical rethinking with brms, ggplot2, and the tidyverse: Second edition](https://bookdown.org/content/4857/) by Solomon Kurz

-   [Regression modelling strategies](https://hbiostat.org/rmsc/)

-   [Stan User's Guide](https://mc-stan.org/docs/stan-users-guide/index.html)

-   [Bayes Rules! An introduction to applied bayesian modelling](https://www.bayesrulesbook.com/)

-   [Tidymodels](https://www.tidymodels.org/)

-   [Beyond Multiple Linear Regression](https://bookdown.org/roback/bookdown-BeyondMLR/)

-   [Statistical Inference via Data Science](https://moderndive.com/)

-   [Improving Your Statistical Inferences](https://lakens.github.io/statistical_inferences/) by Daniel Lakens
:::
:::
:::
